Social Network and Newsfeed

社交网络与新闻动态

Designing a Social Network and Newsfeed System

Social network websites like Twitter (now X), Instagram, and LinkedIn have become vital parts of people’s lives, with most users utilizing them to share information with other people. This information, often referred to as a post on each platform, can be shared as text, images, videos, emojis, and more.

Twitter（现在的 X）、Instagram、LinkedIn 这样的社交网站已经成为人们生活中不可或缺的一部分，大多数用户用它们来与他人分享信息。这种信息在每个平台上通常被称为一条帖子（post），可以以文字、图片、视频、表情符号等形式分享。

Social networking websites offer a variety of features, and we’ll specifically dig deeper into the design of the newsfeed (or user timeline—we’ll use both these terms interchangeably) component of the system. Newsfeed refers to the stream of posts and updates published by other users that a user typically sees as soon as they log into a social media app. Users can interact with these posts via emoji or text responses, or even by sharing the posts on their own feed. The newsfeed for each website can be derived based on different factors. We’ll start our discussion with the system requirements and then proceed to identifying system components to support these requirements. We’ll end the chapter with the potential architecture for our social network newsfeed system on the AWS cloud.

社交网站提供各种各样的功能，我们将专门深入探讨系统中 newsfeed（或用户时间线——这两个术语我们会交替使用）组件的设计。newsfeed 指的是用户一登录社交媒体应用通常看到的、由其他用户发布的帖子和更新的流。用户可以通过表情符号或文字回复与这些帖子互动，甚至可以把帖子转发到自己的 feed 上。每个网站的 newsfeed 可以基于不同因素推导出来。我们将从系统需求开始讨论，然后着手识别支持这些需求的系统组件。本章最后会给出我们在 AWS 云上的社交网络 newsfeed 系统的潜在架构。

System Requirements

Social networking websites offer a variety of features, such as posts that are shared (text, images, videos), a built-in chat messenger, user stories that typically expire in 24 hours, and more. Each feature can be an independent system—for example, the chat messenger, which we’ll discuss in Chapter 19. For now, let’s dig into the functional and nonfunctional requirements of our newsfeed system.

社交网站提供各种各样的功能，例如分享的帖子（文字、图片、视频）、内置的聊天信使、通常在 24 小时后过期的用户 story 等等。每个功能都可以是一个独立的系统——例如聊天信使，我们将在第 19 章讨论。现在，让我们深入探讨 newsfeed 系统的功能需求和非功能需求。

Page 437

Functional and Nonfunctional Requirements

As mentioned before, social networking websites offer a lot of features, so we’ll limit the scope of the design to architect just some of these features for our site. The most important functional requirement in the context of this chapter is reflecting the newsfeed to the user. The newsfeed can be based on a single parameter or a combination of factors, including:

如前所述，社交网站提供很多功能，因此我们把设计范围限定在只为我们的站点架构其中一部分功能。在本章语境下，最重要的功能需求是把 newsfeed 呈现给用户。newsfeed 可以基于单一参数，也可以基于多个因素的组合，包括：

  • All posts associated with a particular hashtag, topic, or location
    与某个特定 hashtag、话题或地点相关的所有帖子
  • All posts published by the people a user is following
    用户关注的人发布的所有帖子
  • All posts liked or shared by the people a user is following
    用户关注的人点赞或分享过的所有帖子
  • All posts derived based on a user’s past interests or assigned priority (for example, breaking news). This involves an ML component, so we’ll skip the details because of space constraints.
    基于用户过去的兴趣或被分配的优先级推导出的所有帖子（例如突发新闻）。这涉及一个 ML 组件，由于篇幅所限我们略过细节。

Our system will create a newsfeed for a user based on people and topics (or hashtags) that the user chooses to follow. We’ll also discuss hashtag-based storage and retrieval of posts (keyword-based search) to some extent in this chapter.

我们的系统将基于用户选择关注的人和话题（或 hashtag）为用户创建 newsfeed。本章我们还会在一定程度上讨论基于 hashtag 的帖子存储与检索（基于关键词的搜索）。

To support the newsfeed feature, the system should inherently support these functional requirements:

为支持 newsfeed 功能，系统本质上应支持以下功能需求：

  • A user onboards to the system and follows (or unfollows) people or topics based on personal interests.
    用户接入系统，并根据个人兴趣关注（或取关）人或话题。
  • A user can make posts (for example, uploading photos in Instagram or posting a text-based post on X).
    用户可以发帖子（例如在 Instagram 上传照片，或在 X 上发文字帖子）。
  • APIs are exposed for retrieving data, which can be useful for monetizing the site. We won’t discuss this requirement in detail, but the idea is for developers to use APIs such as search with keywords or to be able to stream the data of all new posts to interested clients.
    对外暴露用于检索数据的 API，这对站点变现有用。我们不会详细讨论这个需求，但思路是让开发者使用诸如关键词搜索之类的 API，或者能够把所有新帖子的数据流推送给感兴趣的客户端。

Here are the NFRs for the system:

以下是系统的非功能需求（NFR）：

  • The system should be highly available and fault-tolerant to support all of the functional requirements.
    系统应高可用、容错，以支持所有功能需求。
  • Eventual consistency is fine for reflecting posts in the newsfeed. There is acceptable lag between when posts are published by a user and when those posts are reflected in followers’ timelines.
    在 newsfeed 中呈现帖子时，最终一致性即可接受。从用户发布帖子到这些帖子出现在粉丝时间线之间存在可接受的延迟。
  • Keyword search requests should be fast and latency sensitive.
    关键词搜索请求应快速、对延迟敏感。

Let’s discuss the scale of the system next.

接下来讨论系统的规模。

Page 438

System Scale

The number of users interacting with one another on social networking websites like X and Facebook is huge, and our system architecture should handle this increasing scale. Let’s make some assumptions about the scale the system needs to support, starting with the write traffic:

在 X 和 Facebook 这样的社交网站上相互互动的用户数量极其庞大，我们的系统架构应当能够处理这种不断增长的规模。让我们对系统需要支持的规模做一些假设，先从写流量开始：

Number of new posts every second = 10,000
Photos uploaded every second = 800
Videos uploaded every second = 200
Average number of followers per user = 1,000
Maximum number of followers for a user account = 200 million

The read traffic is relatively large compared to the write traffic, so we’ll make these assumptions about the scale:

与写流量相比，读流量相对更大，因此我们对规模做如下假设：

Number of monthly active users on platform = 500 million
User timeline retrieval every second = 100,000

User-interaction traffic, such as liking posts, can be huge; the numbers are in the millions per second. We’ll skip that storage-requirement calculation in this chapter; this can be calculated with scale numbers similar to how we handled it in the previous two chapters.

用户互动流量（例如点赞帖子）可能非常大；数字在每秒数百万级别。本章我们略过那部分存储需求的计算；可以用与前两章类似的规模数字来计算。

Starting with the Design

We’ll not go into depth on onboarding users to the platform as the onboarding system in the entire architecture basically takes care of this. A user onboards with their personal information and then starts following people and topics. Let’s talk a little bit about the storage of follower-following entities so as to ensure that the read queries become efficient. For example, if a user makes a post, that post should be sent to all the user’s followers; we need to ensure that the system can retrieve this follower list quickly and send notifications or populate user timelines.

我们不会深入讨论用户接入平台的过程，因为整个架构中的接入系统基本上已经负责了这件事。用户用个人信息接入，然后开始关注人和话题。让我们稍微讨论一下粉丝—关注关系实体的存储，以确保读查询变得高效。例如，如果一个用户发了帖子，该帖子应被发送给该用户的所有粉丝；我们需要确保系统能快速检索出这份粉丝列表，并发送通知或填充用户时间线。

Relationships between users can be established at multiple levels, not just one-to-one, such as friends of friends, locations, shared interests, and so on. For example, LinkedIn suggests people connections as first, second, and third degree: first degree

用户之间的关系可以在多个层次上建立，而不仅仅是一对一，例如朋友的朋友、地点、共同兴趣等等。例如，LinkedIn 把人脉关系推荐为一度、二度、三度：一度

Page 439

represents people you’re directly connected with, second degree represents a mutual connection, and third degree represents all the user relationships apart from first and second degree. To manage these relationships among users, social networking websites generally leverage graph databases, which we discussed in Chapters 3 and 10. We’ll define a user graph service to manage the user relationships in a graph database. The user graph service can be used in real time by other services to retrieve user followings.

代表你直接连接的人，二度代表共同连接的人，三度代表除一度和二度之外的所有用户关系。为了管理用户之间的这些关系，社交网站通常会利用图数据库，我们在第 3 章和第 10 章讨论过图数据库。我们将定义一个用户图服务，在图数据库中管理用户关系。其他服务可以实时使用该用户图服务来检索用户的关注列表。

Now, let’s talk about the system architecture to handle new post ingestion (creation of new posts by users).

现在，让我们讨论用于处理新帖子接入（用户创建新帖子）的系统架构。

Handling New Posts

The crux of social networking websites is users sharing information with other people. This helps define the goal of the user post service: store posts in such a way that they are sent to other users in near real time. Let’s reiterate the functional requirements of the system:

社交网站的核心是用户与他人分享信息。这帮助我们定义了用户帖子服务的目标：以一种将近实时地把帖子发送给其他用户的方式存储帖子。让我们重申一下系统的功能需求：

  • Allow users to publish new posts and share them with people who are following them.
    允许用户发布新帖子，并分享给关注他们的人。
  • Depending on country or company regulations, post validation is incorporated into the system. Validation can include no hate-speech content, not favoring any political agenda, input sanitization to avoid issues like SQL injection, and the like.
    根据国家或公司法规，系统中内建帖子校验。校验可以包括：不含仇恨言论内容、不偏向任何政治议程、对输入做清洗以避免 SQL 注入之类的问题等等。

Instead of handling validation by the user post service, this responsibility can be given to a frontend service or the user gateway service. The user gateway service runs generic validations (not specific to underlying services) along with other functionalities, such as rate limiting, user authorization and authentication, and request blocking for bad actors.

与其让用户帖子服务处理校验，不如把这个职责交给前端服务或用户网关服务。用户网关服务运行通用校验（不针对底层特定服务）以及其他功能，例如限流、用户授权与认证，以及对恶意行为者的请求拦截。

The way that the user post service storage handles this depends on how the user timeline is built; it can be either a push or a pull mechanism:

用户帖子服务的存储如何处理这件事，取决于用户时间线如何构建；它可以是 push 机制，也可以是 pull 机制：

Push mechanism

The user post service retrieves all followers of a user, builds their timelines, and stores them in a data store. As the user comes online, the user’s timeline can be served directly from the data store.

用户帖子服务检索出某个用户的所有粉丝，构建他们的时间线，并存储在数据存储中。当用户上线时，用户的时间线可以直接从数据存储中返回。

Pull mechanism

The user timeline is built in real time. As the user comes online, the system checks for new posts by people followed by the user and delivers them to the user’s timeline.

用户时间线是实时构建的。当用户上线时，系统检查用户关注的人发布的新帖子，并把它们投递到用户的时间线中。

Page 440

To decide on the approach that would be most beneficial, let’s consider two potential users: user A with 100 followers (a standard user) and user B with 100 million followers (a celebrity user). The push mechanism can work well for users who fall into the user A category, but this would be a lot of ingestion work for celebrity users. The complexity really adds up if the post is tagged with another celebrity or if one celebrity replies to another on the post (X reposts). The push approach makes writes complex (O(n) operation where n is number of followers) in favor of optimizing reads (O(1) operation). The pull mechanism is preferred for celebrity users, and the posts are retrieved in real time while constructing the user timelines.

为了决定哪种方案最有利，让我们考虑两个典型用户：用户 A 有 100 个粉丝（普通用户），用户 B 有 1 亿粉丝（名人用户）。push 机制对属于用户 A 类别的用户很有效，但对名人用户来说这将是大量的接入工作。如果帖子被标记了另一位名人，或者一位名人在帖子下回复另一位名人（X 上的转发），复杂度会进一步叠加。push 方案让写操作变复杂（O(n) 操作，n 是粉丝数），以换取读操作的优化（O(1) 操作）。pull 机制更适合名人用户，帖子在构建用户时间线时实时检索。

It’s worth noting here that if a user follows a lot of celebrity users only and the user timeline is served directly from disk instead of a precomputed cache, then posts will take a relatively longer time to show up in the newsfeed. This is a little hit we can take on customer experience in favor of reducing system complexity. To improve customer experience, social networking websites save older data on the app itself, which is shown on the next visit with background sync in progress to retrieve the latest feed.
这里值得注意的是，如果一个用户只关注了大量名人用户，而用户时间线直接从磁盘（而非预计算缓存）返回，那么帖子出现在 newsfeed 中的时间会相对较长。这是我们为降低系统复杂度而在客户体验上承受的一点小损失。为改善客户体验，社交网站会把较旧的数据保存在应用本地，下次访问时展示这些数据，同时在后台同步拉取最新的 feed。

To make the best of both worlds, we can build a hybrid approach to serve both buckets of users. The user timeline is built consisting of all posts from normal users, and celebrity-user posts are appended in real time while retrieving the user timeline. Let’s talk about the steps in this hybrid architecture in some more detail:

为了兼顾两者的优点，我们可以构建一个混合方案来服务这两类用户。用户时间线由普通用户的所有帖子构建而成，名人用户的帖子则在检索用户时间线时实时追加。让我们更详细地讨论这个混合架构中的步骤：

  1. A user with 10,000+ followers publishes a post with a unique post identifier, the post ID. The post ID is saved to a persistent database like MySQL. We touched on X’s Snowflake in Chapter 14; it can be used here to generate unique post IDs sorted by timestamp.
    一个拥有 1 万以上粉丝的用户发布一条帖子，帖子带有唯一的帖子标识符，即 post ID。post ID 被保存到 MySQL 这样的持久化数据库中。我们在第 14 章提到过 X 的 Snowflake；这里可以用它来生成按时间戳排序的唯一 post ID。
  2. The user post service retrieves all the active follower user IDs from the user graph service to build a timeline in a cache data store for faster retrieval. The cache data store (Redis, for example) stores only the timelines for active users (such as those who last accessed the platform within the past 30 days) and to a certain limit (at the utmost, 30 posts, for example). The rest of the posts are served directly from the on-disk database, and the cache is updated accordingly.
    用户帖子服务从用户图服务检索出所有活跃粉丝的用户 ID，在缓存数据存储中构建时间线以便更快检索。缓存数据存储（例如 Redis）只存储活跃用户的时间线（例如最近 30 天内访问过平台的用户），并且有一定数量上限（例如最多 30 条帖子）。其余帖子直接从磁盘数据库返回，缓存相应地更新。
  3. The cache data store stores only the post IDs against the user IDs. The key-value structure could be something like the key as the user ID and the values as a list (postId, postedBy, and postType). The additional metadata associated with the post, such as the user’s profile picture, likes on the post, and replies associated with the post, can be served independently from a different cache or persistent storage.
    缓存数据存储中只存储用户 ID 对应的 post ID。键值结构可以是这样的：键为用户 ID，值为一个列表（postId、postedBy、postType）。与帖子相关的额外元数据，例如用户头像、帖子的点赞数、帖子的回复，可以独立地从另一个缓存或持久化存储中返回。
Page 441
  1. The user timeline service can directly serve the results from the cache data store for active users and from the on-disk persistent database for inactive users (the cache is updated with the recent timeline once the user becomes active again).
    用户时间线服务对活跃用户可以直接从缓存数据存储返回结果，对不活跃用户则从磁盘持久化数据库返回（一旦用户再次活跃，缓存会用最近的时间线更新）。

Additional components might be involved here, such as ranking and sorting posts depending on the publishing time or user interests, embedding advertisements between posts, and much more. The user timeline service talks to different services (the user service for user information, the post service for post content, and the ranking service for post ranks) and delivers merged results to the user timeline.

这里可能还涉及其他组件，例如根据发布时间或用户兴趣对帖子进行排名和排序、在帖子之间嵌入广告等等。用户时间线服务与不同的服务通信（用户服务提供用户信息、帖子服务提供帖子内容、排名服务提供帖子排名），并把合并后的结果投递到用户时间线。

Figure 16-1 captures the architecture of what happens behind the scenes when a new post is published by a user. We’ve introduced a post workflow orchestration component in the architecture, which is invoked by CDC events once the post is saved to the database and works in asynchronous mode. The orchestration component builds the user’s timeline in cache, and the same new post event can be consumed by the search service to offer search functionality on tags or keywords (more on this in later sections). X works on a similar architecture, which can be referenced from a high-level system diagram published by Elon Musk and the real-time delivery architecture presented at the QCon conference.

图 16-1 展示了当用户发布新帖子时幕后发生的架构。我们在架构中引入了一个帖子工作流编排组件，一旦帖子保存到数据库，该组件就由 CDC 事件触发，并以异步模式工作。编排组件在缓存中构建用户的时间线；同一个新帖子事件也可以被搜索服务消费，以提供基于标签或关键词的搜索功能（后续小节会详细讨论）。X 运行在类似的架构上，可以参考 Elon Musk 发布的高层系统图以及在 QCon 大会上展示的实时投递架构。

User post service databases

The user post service leverages two databases to store the post information: one for storing a post’s structured content (post ID, created by, media metadata) and the other for media content (images and videos). Object storage, such as S3, can be used for storing media content. There is a high probability that the same media is shared by multiple people, and the system should be optimized to handle duplicate content. A simple way to do this could be creating a hash for media content; any new

用户帖子服务利用两个数据库来存储帖子信息：一个存储帖子的结构化内容（post ID、创建者、媒体元数据），另一个存储媒体内容（图片和视频）。对象存储（例如 S3）可用于存储媒体内容。同一个媒体被多个人分享的概率很高，系统应做优化以处理重复内容。一个简单的做法是为媒体内容创建哈希；任何新

Page 442

media uploaded is checked against already uploaded media. We’ll talk more about this in Chapter 19 when we cover the chat application architecture. Another point of consideration is caching media content at edge locations (by leveraging solutions like Amazon CloudFront) to optimize downloads. This helps on two fronts: reducing calls to the user post service and reducing latency for media downloads.

上传的媒体都会与已上传的媒体做比对。我们在第 19 章讨论聊天应用架构时会再详细谈这一点。另一个要考虑的点是在边缘位置缓存媒体内容（利用 Amazon CloudFront 之类的解决方案）以优化下载。这在两方面有帮助：减少对用户帖子服务的调用，以及降低媒体下载的延迟。

Let’s explore both relational and nonrelational kinds of databases to serve the required use case. We can start by identifying the query patterns and expectations from the database engine, which should narrow down the choice. Table 16-1 lists both the read and write query patterns for the user post service.

让我们探讨关系型和非关系型数据库，以满足所需用例。我们可以先识别查询模式以及对数据库引擎的期望，这应该能缩小选择范围。表 16-1 列出了用户帖子服务的读和写查询模式。

WriteRead
Store posts for a userRead all posts by a user
Store comments against a postRead all/paginated comments for a post
Store counters (number of likes, reshares) against a postGet number of likes for a post
Store a list (user ID) of who liked the post; the like type can vary (smile, thumbs up, love, laughter)Get a list of users who liked the post
表 16-1. 用户帖子服务查询模式（中文）
写：为用户存储帖子；为帖子存储评论；为帖子存储计数器（点赞数、转发数）；存储点赞该帖子的用户（用户 ID）列表，点赞类型可以不同（微笑、点赞、爱心、哈哈）。
读：读取某个用户的所有帖子；读取某个帖子的全部/分页评论；获取某个帖子的点赞数；获取点赞该帖子的用户列表。

Both read and write queries are straightforward and can be satisfied by either database choice: a relational database like PostgreSQL (with sharding to support the scale) or a NoSQL database like Amazon DynamoDB or Amazon Keyspaces (compatible with Apache Cassandra). The data in DynamoDB should be stored in a way that makes the read queries efficient, as shown in Table 16-2.

读查询和写查询都很直接，两种数据库选择都能满足：像 PostgreSQL 这样的关系型数据库（配合分片以支持规模），或者像 Amazon DynamoDB 或 Amazon Keyspaces（兼容 Apache Cassandra）这样的 NoSQL 数据库。DynamoDB 中的数据应以一种让读查询高效的方式存储，如表 16-2 所示。

Read querySchema
Read all posts by a userPK = u#{userId}#post  SK = p#{postId}
Read all comments for a postPK = p#{postId}#comments  SK = c#{commentId}
Get number of likes for a postPK = p#{postId}#likeCount  SK = {count}
Get list of users who liked the postPK = p#{postId}#likeList  SK = u#{userId}
Get number of likes for a commentPK = p#{postId}#c#{commentId}#likeCount  SK = {count}
表 16-2. 用户帖子服务读查询对应的 Amazon DynamoDB schema（中文）
读取某用户的所有帖子：PK = u#{userId}#post，SK = p#{postId}；读取某帖子的所有评论：PK = p#{postId}#comments，SK = c#{commentId}；获取帖子点赞数：PK = p#{postId}#likeCount，SK = {count}；获取点赞用户列表：PK = p#{postId}#likeList，SK = u#{userId}；获取评论点赞数：PK = p#{postId}#c#{commentId}#likeCount，SK = {count}。

If a user creates a large number of posts over time and we’re interested in only the most recent, the post ID should either be generated in Snowflake fashion, or it should include a timestamp in the sort key itself, similar to t#{epochTime}#p#{postId} if the post ID is a completely random identifier. Snowflake is our preferred approach because the system requires an implementation for generating unique post IDs at a huge scale.

如果一个用户随时间创建了大量帖子，而我们只关心最新的那些，那么 post ID 要么以 Snowflake 方式生成，要么应在 sort key 本身中包含时间戳，如果 post ID 是完全随机的标识符，类似 t#{epochTime}#p#{postId}。Snowflake 是我们偏爱的方案，因为系统需要一个在超大规模下生成唯一 post ID 的实现。

Page 443
The size of data for a single partition in Amazon DynamoDB is limited to 10 GB, and the defined schema uses the user ID as a partition key. This means we’re assuming that the number of users won’t exceed this limit. The size of a single row is 0.5 KB (with a limit of 400 characters on the lengths of posts), so the maximum number of posts that a user can create is about 20 million.
Amazon DynamoDB 中单个分区的数据大小限制为 10 GB，而定义的 schema 使用用户 ID 作为分区键。这意味着我们假设用户数不会超过这个限制。单行大小为 0.5 KB（帖子长度限制为 400 字符），因此一个用户最多可创建约 2000 万条帖子。

We mentioned that relational databases, such as PostgreSQL, could also be used to store user posts, as shown in Figure 16-2.

我们提到过，关系型数据库（例如 PostgreSQL）也可以用来存储用户帖子，如图 16-2 所示。

The post_id column of the “post like users” and “comments” tables are referenced to the ID of the “posts” table. To support the query pattern of fetching all the comments against a post, an index can be created on post_id for fast retrieval. Considering the scale of the system, the database should be partitioned to support horizontal scaling. We need to figure out a key based on which data can be partitioned into multiple partitions. Consider partitioning logic in the database from the start, if feasible, even though there might not be a requirement for it. The data can be logically partitioned and moved to different physical partitions on a need basis.

“post like users” 表和 “comments” 表的 post_id 列引用到 “posts” 表的 ID。为支持获取某个帖子所有评论的查询模式，可以在 post_id 上创建索引以便快速检索。考虑到系统的规模，数据库应当分区以支持水平扩展。我们需要找出一个键，基于它可以把数据分区到多个分区。如果可行，从一开始就考虑数据库中的分区逻辑，即使目前还没有这个需求。数据可以逻辑分区，并按需移动到不同的物理分区。

For logical partitioning, we recommend a logic similar to how Redis has a hash slot implementation (discussed in Chapter 4). Instagram deploys a similar mechanism for ID generation and for managing logical and physical partitioning by leveraging PostgreSQL features. Another point to note here is that we might be using a relational database, but there is no requirement for strong consistency on features, like managing the number of likes or reflecting all the comments published on a post. These read queries can be eventually consistent to ensure optimal customer experience.

对于逻辑分区，我们推荐一种类似于 Redis hash slot 实现的逻辑（在第 4 章讨论过）。Instagram 利用 PostgreSQL 特性部署了类似的机制来做 ID 生成以及管理逻辑和物理分区。这里要注意的另一点是：我们可能使用的是关系型数据库，但在诸如管理点赞数或呈现某个帖子上发布的所有评论等功能上，并没有强一致性的需求。这些读查询可以是最终一致的，以确保最佳的客户体验。

We mentioned the post workflow orchestration system responsible for fan-out of all posts to the followers and storing them in memory cache. Let’s discuss what goes on behind the scenes in this system and how it scales well for a large number of upcoming posts.

我们提到过帖子工作流编排系统，它负责把所有帖子 fan-out 给粉丝并存储在内存缓存中。让我们讨论一下这个系统幕后发生了什么，以及它如何在大量新帖子到来时良好扩展。

Page 444

Post workflow orchestration and memory cache

The post workflow orchestration is an async layer that comes into the picture once the post from a user is saved to a persistent database. We recommended Redis as a memory cache data store in Figure 16-1 to cache user timelines. Let’s evaluate more on the data store choice here.

帖子工作流编排是一个异步层，一旦用户的帖子保存到持久化数据库中，它就登场了。我们在图 16-1 中推荐 Redis 作为内存缓存数据存储来缓存用户时间线。让我们在这里进一步评估数据存储的选择。

Our primary reason for suggesting Redis is lower latency to serve user queries because data is stored in memory. Redis is faster when compared to any of the on-disk solutions, such as MySQL, Amazon DynamoDB, Cassandra, and the like, which makes it an ideal choice. Another point to note here is the data size requirement—it’s quite huge given the system scale numbers, and this can add to the cost. Is it worth considering databases like DynamoDB or Cassandra? DynamoDB offers automatic horizontal scaling and consistent single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, so it could be a good choice. The final answer to this dilemma is both yes and no, much like any other system design decision we make.

我们建议 Redis 的主要原因是它服务用户查询的延迟更低，因为数据存储在内存中。与任何磁盘上的解决方案（例如 MySQL、Amazon DynamoDB、Cassandra 等）相比，Redis 都更快，这使它成为理想选择。这里要注意的另一点是数据规模需求——考虑到系统规模数字，它相当大，这会增加成本。是否值得考虑 DynamoDB 或 Cassandra 这样的数据库？DynamoDB 提供自动水平扩展，并且在任何规模下都保持个位数毫秒级的一致延迟，因此它也可能是个好选择。这个两难问题的最终答案既是 yes 也是 no，就像我们做的任何其他系统设计决策一样。

In the context of this chapter, we’ll rely on Redis in cluster mode to serve a timeline-caching use case. Revisit Chapter 4 to refresh your understanding of the Redis cluster architecture and how it helps with horizontal scaling with increasing data. We can leverage Redis’s list data structure commands like RPUSHX to always append the entry to the end of the list if the user ID is present in the list (cache only for active users), and LTRIM to keep a fixed-size list of post IDs.

在本章语境下，我们将依赖集群模式下的 Redis 来服务时间线缓存用例。请回顾第 4 章，重温你对 Redis 集群架构以及它如何随数据增长帮助水平扩展的理解。我们可以利用 Redis 的 list 数据结构命令，例如 RPUSHX（如果用户 ID 存在于列表中，则总是把条目追加到列表末尾——只为活跃用户缓存），以及 LTRIM（保持一个固定大小的 post ID 列表）。

Another point to note here with regard to the post workflow orchestrator is pushing the data to the Redis cluster. Assuming every user has an average of 1,000 followers and the system receives 100 posts per second, the number of calls to Redis becomes 100,000. However, the actual number of posts is much larger than 100, and the number of calls to Redis can become a bottleneck in terms of latency and I/O consumption. The ideal approach to solve this kind of problem is batching requests. Redis pipelining can be used to club multiple requests together, gain the benefits of request batching, and address this bottleneck. The bulk requests can be parallelized as well for further optimization.

关于帖子工作流编排器，这里要注意的另一点是把数据推送到 Redis 集群。假设每个用户平均有 1000 个粉丝，系统每秒收到 100 个帖子，那么对 Redis 的调用数就变成 10 万。然而实际帖子数远大于 100，对 Redis 的调用数可能在延迟和 I/O 消耗方面成为瓶颈。解决这类问题的理想方法是批处理请求。Redis pipelining 可以用来把多个请求组合在一起，获得请求批处理的好处，从而解决这个瓶颈。批量请求也可以并行化以进一步优化。

Cache invalidation becomes important for any caching solution we might use. In case a user unfollows someone, the cache should be updated to remove the entry. This again should work in an asynchronous way: any changes in the graph service database are consumed by other components in the architecture and handled per the use case.

对于我们可能使用的任何缓存解决方案，缓存失效都变得重要。如果用户取关了某人，缓存应更新以移除该条目。这同样应以异步方式工作：图服务数据库中的任何变更都被架构中的其他组件消费，并按用例处理。

The memory cache is the first data store to look for to build a user timeline, so let’s discuss that more in the next section.

内存缓存是构建用户时间线时首先查找的数据存储，因此我们在下一节再详细讨论它。

Page 445

User timeline service

Figure 16-3 captures the user timeline service, showing how it gathers data from different components in the architecture to build the user timeline. Memory cache is the first point of lookup for precomputed posts, and additional celebrity posts are retrieved from the user post service. The post ranking service helps with the final sorting and merging of results based on the rank. The query to the user graph service varies based on whether the user is active or not. For active users, the user graph service is queried only to retrieve celebrity users followed by the user, and for nonactive users, the entire list is retrieved and the timeline is built from the on-disk data store.

图 16-3 展示了用户时间线服务，显示它如何从架构中的不同组件收集数据来构建用户时间线。内存缓存是查找预计算帖子的第一站，额外的名人帖子则从用户帖子服务检索。帖子排名服务帮助根据排名对结果做最终排序和合并。对用户图服务的查询根据用户是否活跃而变化。对于活跃用户，只查询用户图服务以检索该用户关注的名人用户；对于不活跃用户，则检索整个列表，时间线从磁盘数据存储构建。

This architecture assumes that no real-time updates are sent to the user applications and that the timeline is updated upon the page refresh. For supporting the requirement of pushing new posts in real time to user timelines, we can explore persistent connections with the user devices. We’ll discuss persistent bidirectional connections in Chapter 19 when we look at the chat application architecture.

这个架构假设不向用户应用发送实时更新，时间线在页面刷新时更新。为支持实时推送新帖子到用户时间线的需求，我们可以探索与用户设备之间的持久连接。我们在第 19 章查看聊天应用架构时会讨论持久双向连接。

We talked about using graph databases for user connections, and we’ve built a basic understanding of graph databases in previous chapters of this book. Let’s dig a little deeper into the architecture of a user graph service and how it works at scale to store so many connections among the users.

我们谈到了使用图数据库来存储用户连接，并且在本书前面的章节中已经建立了对图数据库的基本理解。让我们稍微深入探讨用户图服务的架构，以及它如何在大规模下存储用户之间如此多的连接。

Managing User Connections

The base storage requirement is to manage the followers of each user, essentially managing relationships between the users. Relational databases like MySQL are typically a good choice, so you may be wondering why we recommended a graph database in previous sections. The reason is that the nature of the relations and complex queries need to be served in very low latency—for example, figuring out

基础存储需求是管理每个用户的粉丝，本质上是管理用户之间的关系。像 MySQL 这样的关系型数据库通常是不错的选择，所以你可能想知道为什么我们在前面小节推荐图数据库。原因在于：关系的性质和复杂查询需要以非常低的延迟服务——例如，找出

all the users who follow celebrity A and celebrity B and figuring out second-degree connections for LinkedIn (or mutual friends for Facebook). All of these use cases are well served by a graph database.

同时关注名人 A 和名人 B 的所有用户，以及为 LinkedIn 找出二度人脉（或为 Facebook 找出共同好友）。所有这些用例都能被图数据库很好地服务。

The responsibility of the user graph service is to manage all the relationships. We just mentioned a user-to-user connection relationship, but the relationship can be of any type. Taking the example of LinkedIn, here are a few relationships that can exist between different entities:

用户图服务的职责是管理所有关系。我们刚刚提到了用户到用户的连接关系，但关系可以是任何类型。以 LinkedIn 为例，以下是不同实体之间可能存在的几种关系：

RelationshipMeaning
CONNECTED_TOUser-to-user connections
WORKS_ATThe user’s current organization
WORKED_ATThe user’s past organizations
HAS_SKILLThe user’s skill set
关系含义：CONNECTED_TO（用户到用户的连接）；WORKS_AT（用户当前所在组织）；WORKED_AT（用户过去所在组织）；HAS_SKILL（用户的技能集）。

The user graph service exposes APIs to different services for managing any kind of relationships and publishes events for relationship updates that other services can act on.

用户图服务向不同的服务暴露 API，用于管理任何类型的关系，并发布关系更新事件，供其他服务据此行动。

X uses an in-house solution called EarlyBird (an optimized Lucene index) to support searching. The search service aggregator gathers data from all the instances of EarlyBird matching to the search query. Pagination becomes essential for such use cases because the number of results matching a search query can be huge. We’ll discuss Elasticsearch optimal configurations like shard size in Chapter 18; the same strategy can be leveraged here to build a search system.

X 使用一个名为 EarlyBird（优化版 Lucene 索引）的内部解决方案来支持搜索。搜索服务聚合器从所有与搜索查询匹配的 EarlyBird 实例收集数据。对于这类用例，分页变得至关重要，因为匹配搜索查询的结果数量可能非常庞大。我们将在第 18 章讨论 Elasticsearch 的最佳配置（例如分片大小）；同样的策略可以在这里用来构建搜索系统。

The use cases for searching are many, and there is a need to define the boundaries of what a system is built to support. For example, search for “breakfast recipes” in Instagram, and it presents different types of results in defined sections: “for you” (search results relevant for the user); account names with a breakfast item as the identifier; audio, or music associated with breakfast; tags, or keywords with a breakfast name; and places and reels targeted around “breakfast” as a keyword. Now notice that this search is very fast (along with offering you type-ahead search options), and all these results are rendered very quickly. The amount of data stored on Instagram servers is huge, so the indexing strategy should be quite efficient to power the search functionality at scale.

搜索的用例很多，因此需要定义系统被构建来支持的边界。例如，在 Instagram 中搜索“早餐食谱”，它会在定义好的分区中呈现不同类型的结果：“为你推荐”（与用户相关的搜索结果）；以早餐食品为标识的账号名；与早餐相关的音频或音乐；带有早餐名称的标签或关键词；以及以“早餐”为关键词定向的地点和 reel。现在注意这个搜索非常快（同时还提供输入时的联想搜索选项），所有这些结果都渲染得非常快。Instagram 服务器上存储的数据量巨大，因此索引策略必须非常高效，才能在大规模下支撑搜索功能。

Launching the System on AWS

The most important consideration for deploying a social networking website is user interaction availability. We should consider how to ensure this when choosing any AWS service. We spent a good amount of time on building systems for handling new posts to make sure the user read paths are optimal. Another consideration for the nature of the system is eventually consistent behavior, giving us the ability to improve on cost and latency. We’ll start with the Day 0 architecture of the system and then try to scale for a larger user base.

部署社交网站时最重要的考量是用户交互可用性。在选择任何 AWS 服务时都应考虑如何确保这一点。我们花了相当多时间构建处理新帖子的系统，以确保用户读路径是最优的。该系统性质的另一个考量是最终一致行为，这让我们有能力在成本和延迟上做优化。我们将从系统的 Day 0 架构开始，然后尝试扩展到更大的用户群。

Day 0 Architecture

We’ll design a very basic system to support requirements like uploading of posts by users and ensuring that followers can see these posts in their timelines. The DynamoDB schema from Table 16-2 can be extended to include user information and followers, as shown in Table 16-3.

我们将设计一个非常基础的系统，以支持用户上传帖子、并确保粉丝能在自己的时间线中看到这些帖子等需求。表 16-2 中的 DynamoDB schema 可以扩展为包含用户信息和粉丝，如表 16-3 所示。

Query patternSchema
User information with counters (number of followers, following, posts)PK = u#{userId}  SK = count
User followersPK = u#{userId}#followers  SK = u#{followerUserId}
User followingPK = u#{userId}#following  SK = u#{followingUserId}
表 16-3. Amazon DynamoDB 中的用户信息（中文）
带计数器的用户信息（粉丝数、关注数、帖子数）：PK = u#{userId}，SK = count；用户粉丝：PK = u#{userId}#followers，SK = u#{followerUserId}；用户关注：PK = u#{userId}#following，SK = u#{followingUserId}。

A single DynamoDB table serves our storage needs and supports all of the query patterns. We can build the keyword search functionality on top of DynamoDB by streaming the user post data to an Amazon OpenSearch cluster via DynamoDB streams, as shown in Figure 16-5.

单个 DynamoDB 表就能满足我们的存储需求，并支持所有查询模式。我们可以在 DynamoDB 之上构建关键词搜索功能：通过 DynamoDB streams 把用户帖子数据流到 Amazon OpenSearch 集群，如图 16-5 所示。

This architecture comprises multiple AWS Lambda functions to serve different use cases, as is evident from their names. The transformation Lambda converts DynamoDB data objects to an OpenSearch schema and makes them available for search. This doesn’t introduce a separate caching layer, but we can add that as and when required in the form of Amazon DAX or Amazon ElastiCache. We can use Amazon SNS and Amazon SES to deliver notifications to the users, and we can integrate monitoring tools like Amazon CloudWatch for application monitoring and issue debugging.

这个架构包含多个 AWS Lambda 函数来服务不同用例，从它们的名字就能看出。转换 Lambda 把 DynamoDB 数据对象转换为 OpenSearch schema，并使其可搜索。这里没有引入单独的缓存层，但我们可以在需要时以 Amazon DAX 或 Amazon ElastiCache 的形式加上。我们可以使用 Amazon SNS 和 Amazon SES 向用户投递通知，并可以集成 Amazon CloudWatch 之类的监控工具来做应用监控和问题调试。

Page 449

We skipped the analytics pipeline entirely in the Day 0 architecture; it could be helpful for running complex queries to derive data insights with tools like Amazon Redshift and Amazon QuickSight. The integration can be like data ingestion to an Amazon OpenSearch cluster; a separate Lambda can convert the data to a Redshift schema and save it to the cluster.

在 Day 0 架构中我们完全略过了分析管道；它对于用 Amazon Redshift 和 Amazon QuickSight 之类的工具运行复杂查询以获得数据洞见可能很有帮助。集成方式可以类似到 Amazon OpenSearch 集群的数据接入；一个单独的 Lambda 可以把数据转换为 Redshift schema 并保存到集群中。

Scaling to Millions and Beyond

The scale of social networking websites is huge, and delivering a fast, reliable user experience is of utmost importance. We’ll explore many considerations for scaling the architecture throughout the rest of this book, and we recommend taking learnings from all of them. We have already included scalable architecture as part of Figures 16-1 and 16-3; in this section, we’ll discuss scaling the architecture further on AWS. Let’s start with a few of the storage choices we have made previously in this chapter.

社交网站的规模巨大，交付快速、可靠的用户体验至关重要。我们将在本书剩余部分探讨架构扩展的诸多考量，并建议你从所有这些内容中汲取经验。我们已经在图 16-1 和图 16-3 中包含了可扩展架构；在本节中，我们将讨论在 AWS 上进一步扩展架构。让我们从本章前面做出的几个存储选择开始。

Storage on DynamoDB

Table 16-3 shows the DynamoDB schema for storing a user’s information, such as the users that they are following and their followers. We introduced the concept of hot keys in “Amazon DynamoDB” on page 265 in Chapter 10 and made some recommendations to resolve this issue. The suggested DynamoDB schema uses user ID as the partition key, meaning the following and followers data should fit into the

表 16-3 展示了用于存储用户信息的 DynamoDB schema，例如该用户关注的人及其粉丝。我们在第 10 章第 265 页“Amazon DynamoDB”一节中介绍了热键（hot key）的概念，并给出了解决该问题的一些建议。建议的 DynamoDB schema 使用用户 ID 作为分区键，这意味着关注和粉丝数据应能放入

Page 450

limit of 10 GB per user. Some potential problems that can occur with scale, especially for celebrity users, include:

每个用户 10 GB 的限制内。随着规模增长可能出现的一些潜在问题（尤其是对名人用户）包括：

Partition storage limit

Assuming a storage requirement of 100 bytes for keeping a single follower’s data, a celebrity user can have approximately 107 million followers before breaching the 10 GB limit. Revisit Chapter 10 for recommendations on partitioning the data further for a partition that has already been created.

假设保存单个粉丝的数据需要 100 字节的存储，一个名人用户在突破 10 GB 限制之前大约可以有 1.07 亿粉丝。请回顾第 10 章，了解对已创建分区进一步分区数据的建议。

Read and write capacity limit

DynamoDB throttles the request if a partition has a hard limit of 3,000 RCUs or 1,000 WCUs (or both). The throttling can affect the read/write for count operations that we suggested for managing following and followers count in Table 16-3. This can happen if the user’s followers increase or decrease in a spiky workload situation, such as a celebrity gaining popularity after a big endorsement or a falling out of favor due to a public backlash. The problem statement is similar to managing the number of likes for a post or the number of comments on a post. The guiding principle for serving this requirement is eventual consistency. Instead of direct writes to the table, the data should be persisted with a messaging queue in between, and reads should be served from the cache instead of directly hitting the table, as shown in Figure 16-6.

如果一个分区达到了 3000 RCU 或 1000 WCU（或两者）的硬限制，DynamoDB 会对请求限流。限流可能影响我们在表 16-3 中建议用于管理关注数和粉丝数的计数操作的读/写。当用户的粉丝在尖峰负载情况下增加或减少时可能发生这种情况，例如一位名人在一次大型代言后人气上升，或因公众强烈反对而失宠。这个问题陈述与管理帖子点赞数或帖子评论数类似。服务这个需求的指导原则是最终一致性。数据不应直接写入表中，而应在中间加一个消息队列来持久化；读操作应从缓存返回，而不是直接打到表上，如图 16-6 所示。

We’ve showcased the user post service in the context of managing the likes count, and a similar pattern is applicable for the number of followers. The write operation can be optimized further by batching multiple requests together; instead of incrementing the like count by one every time, multiple requests can be batched together and updated in one go, reducing database workload.

我们在管理点赞数的语境下展示了用户帖子服务，类似的模式也适用于粉丝数。写操作可以通过把多个请求批处理在一起进一步优化；不是每次把点赞数加 1，而是把多个请求批处理在一起一次性更新，从而降低数据库负载。

We discussed the push versus pull mechanism for celebrity users in the context of post creation in “Handling New Posts” on page 418. A similar design problem occurs for the comments published against a post at high scale.

我们在第 418 页“处理新帖子”一节中，在帖子创建语境下讨论了名人用户的 push 与 pull 机制。在大规模下，针对某个帖子发布评论时也会出现类似的设计问题。

Page 451

Scaling post comments

We’re fine with eventual consistency for the read paths, so the recommendation is comments served using memory cache and in paginated form. An important point to address is that when a user publishes a comment, they should see it with causal consistency, as discussed in Chapter 1. The comment should not disappear due to eventual consistency; this could create confusion about whether it was successfully posted.

我们对读路径采用最终一致性是可以接受的，因此建议评论使用内存缓存并以分页形式返回。一个要解决的重点是：当用户发布一条评论时，他们应以因果一致性看到它，如第 1 章所讨论的。评论不应因最终一致性而消失；这会让人困惑它是否成功发布了。

One way to address this problem is by handling this behavior in the frontend application (user app or web browser). The application makes an API call to the server for publishing a comment. Upon a successful API response, the comment is cached on the app itself and shown at the top. This is the simplest implementation for a smooth user experience, and a similar design is followed by the social media platforms for the user timeline. The application caches the content on local devices until the response is updated from the servers.

解决这个问题的一种方法是在前端应用（用户 app 或网页浏览器）中处理这种行为。应用向服务器发起 API 调用来发布评论。API 成功响应后，评论被缓存在应用本地，并显示在顶部。这是获得流畅用户体验的最简单实现，社交媒体平台在用户时间线上也采用类似设计。应用把内容缓存在本地设备上，直到服务器更新了响应。

Skip the idea of handling it on the user app for a while—let’s think how this can be addressed at the database level. This discussion is important for making decisions in similar problems statements. So the issue is that the user should see a consistent view of data on the application. The simplest implementation is directing all the queries to the leader node where writes are happening (or specifying ConsistentRead as true in the DynamoDB API), but this increases the load on the database. A helpful idea in this situation is “read your write” consistency.

暂时先不考虑在用户 app 上处理的思路——让我们想想如何在数据库层面解决。这个讨论对于在类似问题陈述中做决策很重要。问题在于用户应在应用上看到一致的数据视图。最简单的实现是把所有查询都导向正在写入的 leader 节点（或在 DynamoDB API 中指定 ConsistentRead 为 true），但这会增加数据库的负载。在这种情况下一个有用的思路是“读己之写”（read your write）一致性。

To achieve “read your write” consistency, the user should be tied to the leader node (or enable consistent reads for required operations) for the time being, depending on the time taken for the data replication in the database cluster. Synchronous replication is another way to ensure that all the database nodes have the same view, but it comes with a huge latency cost and is not recommended for write-heavy use cases.

要实现“读己之写”一致性，应根据数据库集群中数据复制所花费的时间，暂时把用户绑定到 leader 节点（或对所需操作启用一致性读）。同步复制是确保所有数据库节点拥有相同视图的另一种方式，但它带来巨大的延迟代价，不建议用于写密集型用例。

Let’s also talk a little bit about reads. The ratio of content producers to consumers is very skewed; the scale of reads is exponentially high compared to the writes. Social platforms generally work on the principle of live comments, meaning that comments are pushed to user devices automatically without refreshing the app or web browser. To support this design, either a user device continuously polls for new updates or the server pushes the updates automatically. A poll-based approach can work at a smaller scale, but it can become a bottleneck with increasing scale. A continuous poll (it should be less than five seconds for near real-time behavior) can overload the backend servers and is not a recommended approach. A system with a push-based approach figures out which viewers are looking at the content and sends the updates to their devices.

我们也稍微谈谈读。内容生产者与消费者的比例非常倾斜；读的规模与写相比呈指数级高出。社交平台通常按实时评论的原则运作，意味着评论会自动推送到用户设备，无需刷新 app 或网页浏览器。为支持这种设计，要么用户设备持续轮询新更新，要么服务器自动推送更新。基于轮询的方法在较小规模下可行，但随着规模增长可能成为瓶颈。持续轮询（要达到近实时行为应小于 5 秒）可能压垮后端服务器，不是推荐的方法。基于 push 的系统会弄清楚哪些观看者正在看内容，并把更新发送到他们的设备。

The requirement is similar to group messaging for chat applications and is generally solved by managing persistent connections with users’ devices. We’ll dive deep into

这个需求类似于聊天应用的群消息，通常通过管理与用户设备的持久连接来解决。我们将在

Page 452

chat application design in Chapter 19, with all the architectural nitty-gritty, but let’s discuss a shorter way to push comments to all the interested viewers for a particular post, illustrated in Figure 16-7.

第 19 章深入探讨聊天应用设计的所有架构细节，但这里我们先讨论一种更简短的方式，把评论推送给某个特定帖子的所有感兴趣观看者，如图 16-7 所示。

Once a comment is published by a user, it is saved locally in the regional database. There is asynchronous replication as well for database writes in one more region for data redundancy, which is discussed in “Multiregion deployments” on page 438. The comment is pushed to the queue for fanning out to all the regions. The regional deployment of the gateway service figures out all the users subscribed to a post and routes the comment to all the user devices.

一旦用户发布了评论，它就被保存在本地区域数据库中。数据库写入还会异步复制到另一个区域以做数据冗余，这在第 438 页“多区域部署”一节中讨论。评论被推入队列，以便 fan-out 到所有区域。网关服务的区域部署会找出订阅了某个帖子的所有用户，并把评论路由到所有用户设备。

The authentication and authorization system is another critical component for any system we design. Let’s discuss it in the context of scaling the system for millions of customers.

认证与授权系统是我们设计的任何系统的另一个关键组件。让我们在把系统扩展到数百万客户的语境下讨论它。

Scaling the authentication system

We’ll specifically focus on AuthN and AuthZ and discuss Amazon Cognito scalability and whether it’s a good idea to use it at our proposed scale instead of developing a custom solution. We introduced Cognito’s offerings and related concepts in Chapter 12, and see that chapter to get the most out of the comparison discussion here. The main idea behind choosing managed services such as Cognito is removing the entire development and operational burden from your plate and letting AWS manage the service end to end.

我们将专门关注 AuthN 和 AuthZ，讨论 Amazon Cognito 的可扩展性，以及在我们提出的规模下使用它（而非开发自定义解决方案）是否是个好主意。我们在第 12 章介绍了 Cognito 的产品和相关概念，参见那一章以充分理解这里的比较讨论。选择像 Cognito 这样的托管服务背后的主要思路，是把整个开发和运维负担从你肩上卸下来，让 AWS 端到端管理该服务。

Security solutions are hard to build and require expertise to build them right because even though the application is operating at a lower scale, you can’t compromise on

安全解决方案很难构建，需要专业知识才能构建正确，因为即使应用在较低规模下运行，你也不能在

Page 453

customers’ personal data. Table 16-4 compares various aspects of Cognito and a custom authentication service.

客户个人数据上妥协。表 16-4 比较了 Cognito 与自定义认证服务的各个方面。

Comparison aspectAmazon CognitoCustom solution
Security featuresCognito comes with multiple features for AuthN and AuthZ, as discussed in Chapter 12. Cognito allows customization to a great extent, but you still don’t have end-to-end flexibility over how the system works internally.Custom solutions require security expertise to build an end-to-end solution. If there is a limitation to using Cognito in any of the aspects, there is an option to build the auth application by self-hosting open source software like Keycloak and amending the code per custom needs.
Security expertiseBuilding solutions to secure your systems takes expertise, and Cognito helps take that off your plate. You don’t have to worry about security features and scalability; you can simply focus on the business logic of the software.(same row)—see left.
Operations: managing compute and storageCognito scales automatically as needed, and no user intervention is required.The custom solution requires proper scaling strategies as the business grows.
Compliance regulations, such as HIPAA and PCI DSSCognito is compliant with these standards. While Cognito supports multiple compliance regulations, if any country compliance isn’t supported, then custom solutions make more sense.The compliance requirements need to be inherently built in custom solutions.
Multiregion availabilityCognito doesn’t offer multiregion support out of the box, which adds extra overhead at the customer’s end for managing multiregion users.Custom solutions can be deployed or replicated across the required regions as needed.
Integration with AWS servicesCognito makes it very easy to integrate with other AWS services, such as Amazon API Gateway and AWS ALB.Integration requires additional effort for a custom solution.
Migration to another cloud provider, going entirely on-premises, or migrating to a different auth serviceMigration can be very tricky with cloud-specific auth solutions. The migration requires figuring out the auth service in another cloud, and it’s often a major headache to migrate existing users to a new cloud. Cognito doesn’t allow export of user passwords and becomes a bottleneck in migration (you can get around it by authenticating a user via Cognito and forcing them to reset the password; this can work well with active users but is not straightforward for inactive users).A custom application is easy to migrate to different clouds as long as the compute and storage solutions are cloud agnostic. The extra effort is needed only in situations like moving from Amazon DynamoDB in the AWS cloud to Spanner in the Google cloud.
表 16-4. Amazon Cognito 与自定义认证方案对比（中文）
安全特性：Cognito 自带多种 AuthN/AuthZ 特性（见第 12 章），允许高度定制，但仍无法端到端控制系统内部工作方式；自定义方案需要安全专家构建端到端方案，若 Cognito 在某方面有限制，可自托管 Keycloak 等开源软件并按需要改代码。
安全专业能力：构建保护系统的方案需要专业知识，Cognito 帮你卸下这副担子，你只需关注业务逻辑。
运维（计算与存储管理）：Cognito 按需自动扩展，无需人工干预；自定义方案需随业务增长制定扩展策略。
合规（如 HIPAA、PCI DSS）：Cognito 已合规；若某国合规要求不被支持，则自定义方案更合理。自定义方案需内建合规要求。
多区域可用性：Cognito 不原生提供多区域支持，增加客户管理多区域用户的开销；自定义方案可按需跨区域部署或复制。
与 AWS 服务集成：Cognito 与 Amazon API Gateway、AWS ALB 等集成非常容易；自定义方案需额外投入。
迁移到其他云/全本地/换认证服务：云特定认证方案迁移很棘手，Cognito 不允许导出用户密码，成为迁移瓶颈（可通过 Cognito 认证后强制重置密码绕过，活跃用户可行，不活跃用户不直接）；自定义应用只要计算和存储方案与云无关就容易迁移，仅在从 DynamoDB 迁到 Spanner 这类情况需要额外工作。

Go through this comparison and identify which aspects best match your needs.

仔细看看这个对比，找出哪些方面最符合你的需求。

Session management is one of the features we require so that the user doesn’t have to go through authentication flow again and again. JWTs are a way to make session management easier. The idea is that once a user is authenticated by the system, subsequent calls to the system should not require AuthN and AuthZ to speed up

会话管理是我们需要的功能之一，这样用户就不必反复走认证流程。JWT 是让会话管理更简单的一种方式。思路是：一旦用户被系统认证，后续对系统的调用就不应再要求 AuthN 和 AuthZ，以加速

Page 454

the operations (depending on the system architecture, authentication might require talking to an auth service or performing a database lookup to validate the user credentials). JWTs allow users to create a token once they are authenticated for the first time. Subsequent calls to the system are required to pass on this token, and the system validates the user based on this token. This operation is done in memory of the application servers and speeds up the API operations; the API can skip the authorization against specific resources and just focus on executing application logic.

操作（取决于系统架构，认证可能需要与认证服务通信或做数据库查询来验证用户凭据）。JWT 允许用户在首次认证后创建一个 token。后续对系统的调用必须携带这个 token，系统基于该 token 验证用户。这个操作在应用服务器内存中完成，加速了 API 操作；API 可以跳过针对特定资源的授权，只专注于执行业务逻辑。

This looks great, but there is no such thing as a free lunch, so what’s the catch? The catch is the token expiration time: assume the token expiration is set to five minutes, but the user logs out within one minute. In these scenarios, the token can be misused by man-in-the-middle attacks for the next four minutes, opening the system to security threats. Redis has documented this potential threat in its engineering blog and recommends using traditional database lookups for user authentication and limiting JWT to service-to-service communications.

这看起来很棒，但天下没有免费的午餐，那陷阱是什么？陷阱就是 token 过期时间：假设 token 过期设为 5 分钟，但用户在 1 分钟内就登出了。在这种场景下，接下来的 4 分钟里 token 可能被中间人攻击滥用，使系统暴露于安全威胁。Redis 在其工程博客中记录了这一潜在威胁，并建议用户认证使用传统的数据库查询，把 JWT 限制在服务间通信。

We know we keep repeating the phrase “It depends on the business use case,” but this holds true here as well. Evaluate the requirements of the system and not blindly settling on any technology. For example, don’t assume JWT is a bad choice after reading the previous paragraph; every technology has pros and cons.

我们知道我们一直在重复“这取决于业务用例”这句话，但在这里同样成立。评估系统的需求，不要盲目选定任何技术。例如，不要读了上一段就认为 JWT 是个糟糕的选择；每种技术都有优缺点。

Moving from Day 0 to Day N

As companies grow over time, their engineering teams create optimizations on top of existing software or develop new software altogether to support the scale and system features. This should be evaluated from time to time and can heavily depend on the business use case you’re trying to solve. Social networking giants like X and Facebook have built multiple technologies to support scale and have made some of them open source. See the documentation of these software applications (refer to the engineering blogs of the companies) to understand the problem statement and solution and gain a deeper understanding of different components in the architecture.

随着公司随时间成长，其工程团队会在现有软件之上做优化，或者完全开发新软件来支持规模和系统功能。这一点应不时评估，并很大程度上取决于你要解决的业务用例。像 X 和 Facebook 这样的社交巨头构建了多种技术来支持规模，并把其中一些开源了。查看这些软件应用的文档（参考各公司的工程博客），以理解问题陈述和解决方案，并更深入地理解架构中的不同组件。

For example, X has developed FlockDB for distributed graph storage, Gizzard for managing data partitioning, and Manhattan as a multitenant distributed graph database. Similarly, Facebook has developed Unicorn for searching trillions of edges in the social graph (Instagram uses Unicorn to power the search infrastructure) and Haystack as object storage for multimedia content, and it has optimized Memcached for caching at Facebook scale. You can find similar innovations from other companies as well. For example, LinkedIn built its in-house graph database called LIquid to support multidegree connections.

例如，X 开发了 FlockDB 用于分布式图存储、Gizzard 用于管理数据分区、Manhattan 作为多租户分布式图数据库。类似地，Facebook 开发了 Unicorn 用于在社交图中搜索数万亿条边（Instagram 使用 Unicorn 来驱动搜索基础设施），Haystack 作为多媒体内容的对象存储，并针对 Facebook 规模优化了 Memcached。你也能从其他公司找到类似的创新。例如，LinkedIn 构建了内部图数据库 LIquid 来支持多度人脉。

Page 455

Once an improved system is built, the traffic should be seamlessly transitioned to this new system without affecting end users. The strategy of migration can vary depending on multiple factors, such as the following:

一旦改进后的系统构建完成，流量应无缝切换到这个新系统，而不影响终端用户。迁移策略可以因多种因素而不同，例如：

  • Migration happens with downtime, and the application is not available in a certain time window. The migration process becomes much more complex if it should be completed without any downtime.
    迁移在停机情况下进行，应用在某个时间窗口内不可用。如果迁移必须在零停机情况下完成，迁移过程会复杂得多。
  • Whether the system is stateless or stateful: stateless systems are relatively easier to migrate as there is no state saved on the server instance and it is maintained in a database on a different hardware machine. Stateful systems maintain a backend system and database on a single hardware machine. We’ll discuss an example of a stateful system in Chapter 19.
    系统是无状态还是有状态：无状态系统相对容易迁移，因为服务器实例上不保存状态，状态维护在另一台硬件机器的数据库中。有状态系统在单台硬件机器上维护后端系统和数据库。我们将在第 19 章讨论一个有状态系统的例子。

Let’s discuss different strategies we can follow for smooth migration.

让我们讨论可以遵循的不同平滑迁移策略。

Traffic replication on the new system.  We need a mechanism for gaining confidence in the working of the new system, and the best way is to put this system to work. The work for the system is serving actual production traffic. Once developer or quality assurance testing is completed, the system should be tested against real production traffic, as shown in Figure 16-8.

在新系统上复制流量。我们需要一种机制来建立对新系统工作的信心，最好的方式就是让这个系统真正工作起来。系统的工作就是服务真实的生产流量。一旦开发或 QA 测试完成，就应让系统对着真实生产流量测试，如图 16-8 所示。

The existing system both processes the request and forwards the same request to the new system. The response analysis pipeline compares these two responses and generates metrics for verification. To ensure the same process can be leveraged by other teams in the organization, we can create a separate service component responsible for replaying the traffic to the new system and verify the results.

现有系统既处理请求，又把同一个请求转发给新系统。响应分析管道比较这两个响应并生成用于验证的指标。为确保组织中其他团队也能利用同一流程，我们可以创建一个单独的服务组件，负责把流量重放到新系统并验证结果。

Page 456

Note that the customers are still served by the existing system; the new system is just working in parallel for confidence. To start, the new system is exposed to a portion of the production system and is gradually scaled for all the production traffic. Any issues encountered are fixed along the way.

注意，客户仍然由现有系统服务；新系统只是并行工作以建立信心。一开始，新系统只暴露给生产系统的一部分，然后逐步扩展到全部生产流量。遇到的任何问题都在过程中修复。

Actual system migration.  Once we’re sure the new system is working as expected, we can expose the new system to serve the actual production traffic. This is again done in stages to ensure smooth migration; a strategy for user-facing applications is shown in Figure 16-9.

真正的系统迁移。一旦我们确信新系统按预期工作，就可以让新系统服务真实生产流量。这同样分阶段进行以确保平滑迁移；面向用户的应用的策略如图 16-9 所示。

A/B testing is a popular strategy that works in a similar fashion. You design experiments and divide the traffic accordingly based on traffic division logic; one such logic is shown in Figure 16-8.

A/B 测试是一种流行的策略，以类似方式工作。你设计实验，并根据流量划分逻辑相应地划分流量；图 16-8 展示了一种这样的逻辑。

Once the application works well with a limited set of user groups, we can move to a percentage-wise rollout. We can start with as little as 1% of the traffic and gradually move to 10%, 30%, 50%, and so on. After a 100% rollout of the new system, we recommend letting it run for about two weeks and then deciding when to turn off the old system.

一旦应用在有限用户组下运行良好，我们就可以转向按百分比灰度发布。我们可以从低至 1% 的流量开始，逐步到 10%、30%、50% 等等。新系统 100% 发布后，我们建议让它运行约两周，然后再决定何时关闭旧系统。

Migration is a relatively easier process if no database migration is involved, but if this is not the case, let’s discuss some recommendations to handle that.

如果不涉及数据库迁移，迁移是相对容易的过程；但如果涉及，让我们讨论一些处理建议。

Database migration.  Database migration can involve moving from an older data model to a newer data model on the same database engine or a data-model upgrade and a change of database engine, such as moving from PostgreSQL to DynamoDB. Here are a few tips for a smooth database migration:

数据库迁移。数据库迁移可以是在同一数据库引擎上从旧数据模型迁移到新数据模型，也可以是数据模型升级并更换数据库引擎，例如从 PostgreSQL 迁到 DynamoDB。以下是平滑数据库迁移的几个技巧：
  • The older data needs to be moved to a newer database model. This can be done by offline batch loads using a transformation layer, which converts older model data to newer model data.
    旧数据需要迁移到新的数据库模型。这可以通过转换层做离线批量加载来完成，转换层把旧模型数据转换为新模型数据。
  • During the migration window, the system should follow a dual write strategy. This means the data should be written to both databases.
    在迁移窗口期间，系统应遵循双写策略。这意味着数据应同时写入两个数据库。
  • The read strategy is also dual. This means the system reads data from both the databases. An extra verification layer can be added that compares the data from both databases for validation. This holds true if the database migration is only involved within the same system; if there is an entirely new architecture
    读策略也是双份的。这意味着系统从两个数据库读取数据。可以增加一个额外的验证层，比较来自两个数据库的数据以做校验。如果数据库迁移只发生在同一系统内，这成立；如果是一个全新的架构
Page 457
  • with a different database, the verification can happen at the API request level, as discussed in previous sections.
    使用不同的数据库，则验证可以在 API 请求层面进行，如前面小节所讨论。

The last step for any type of migration is clearing up the old resources. The old architecture should be tiered down to remove any operational burden and save the cost of unused resources.

任何类型迁移的最后一步是清理旧资源。旧架构应逐步下线，以消除运维负担并节省未使用资源的成本。

Day N Architecture

The scope of building a user timeline can grow over time and can include additional posts based on interests, location, or any other particular parameters. The primary requirement for building a timeline is to show all posts from the people a user is following, and additional components can be added as the system evolves. The Day N architecture based on all the discussion in this chapter is presented in Figure 16-10.

构建用户时间线的范围可以随时间增长，可以包含基于兴趣、地点或任何其他特定参数的额外帖子。构建时间线的首要需求是展示用户关注的人的所有帖子，随着系统演进可以添加额外组件。基于本章所有讨论的 Day N 架构如图 16-10 所示。

We skipped Amazon CloudFront in the architecture diagram for simplification, but the idea is to serve media content from a CDN instead of downloading it directly from the S3 bucket. We’ll discuss multiple content distribution strategies as part of Chapter 20. We touched on the orchestration component in Chapter 15, and we can use the same reference here.

为简化起见，我们在架构图中略去了 Amazon CloudFront，但思路是从 CDN 提供媒体内容，而不是直接从 S3 桶下载。我们将在第 20 章讨论多种内容分发策略。我们在第 15 章提到过编排组件，这里可以引用同一参考。

We should identify the critical components of the system for operating and for serving the users; ranking the posts at user level or adding more posts are extras that we’re building to keep users engaged. Let’s elaborate more on this idea and how it can help achieve high availability for the systems in the overall architecture.

我们应识别系统中用于运维和服务用户的关键组件；在用户层面对帖子排名或添加更多帖子，是我们为保持用户粘性而构建的额外功能。让我们详细阐述这个思路，以及它如何帮助在整体架构中为系统实现高可用。

Page 458

High availability of system

In case of any unforeseen instances, such as cloud provider services going down or increased load due to a retry storm with newly introduced code, the system architecture should ensure that end users are least impacted. We should perform multiple levels of testing from time to time to ensure that the issues are identified beforehand, but let’s discuss some recommendations for how to plan better if this situation does occur.

在任何不可预见的情况下（例如云服务商服务宕机，或因新引入代码导致的重试风暴而负载增加），系统架构应确保终端用户受到的影响最小。我们应不时执行多级测试，以确保问题被提前识别；但让我们讨论一些建议，万一这种情况真的发生时如何更好地规划。

Page 459

The first recommendation involves identifying the criticality of the application. All the subsystems in the architecture are assigned a certain level of priority; for example Amazon follows a tier structure: Tier 1 means a highly critical system with direct impact on the customer, Tier 2 means a medium-critical system with medium impact (for example, an order is delayed by one day but is still delivered), and Tier 3 means a low-critical system that provides an add-on experience. This division helps Amazon focus only on Tier 1 systems in case of downtime and further makes it mandatory for these systems to go through extra steps of testing before any new changes are made live.

第一个建议涉及识别应用的关键性。架构中的所有子系统都被分配了某个优先级级别；例如 Amazon 遵循一个层级结构：Tier 1 表示高度关键的系统，对客户有直接影响；Tier 2 表示中等关键的系统，影响中等（例如订单延迟一天但仍送达）；Tier 3 表示低关键系统，提供附加体验。这种划分帮助 Amazon 在宕机时只关注 Tier 1 系统，并进一步强制这些系统在任何新变更上线前经过额外的测试步骤。

Another suggestion in the same vein involves identifying requests that need to be processed based on priority and dropping nonpriority requests. Let’s take an example from Netflix’s systems. Two types of requests are sent to the API gateway: playback requests and telemetry requests. Telemetry requests send the health metrics from the user devices, which are helpful for improving the user experience, but playback requests are most critical because they serve the content. Based on the health metrics, a system state can be identified beforehand, and the gateway drops the request instead of building up the request queue of the system.

另一个类似的建议涉及根据优先级识别需要处理的请求，并丢弃非优先级请求。让我们从 Netflix 的系统举个例子。发送到 API 网关的请求有两种：播放请求和遥测请求。遥测请求从用户设备发送健康指标，这对改善用户体验有帮助，但播放请求最关键，因为它们服务内容。基于健康指标，可以提前识别系统状态，网关直接丢弃请求，而不是让系统的请求队列堆积。

An important consideration for large systems is deployment across regions. Let’s discuss multiregion deployments in more detail.

对于大型系统，一个重要考量是跨区域部署。让我们更详细地讨论多区域部署。

Multiregion deployments

Managing an application on such a large scale comes with a lot of challenges, and expanding the application to multiple regions brings a new set of issues. There can be different reasons why companies choose this kind of deployment strategy:

在如此大规模下管理应用伴随着许多挑战，把应用扩展到多个区域会带来一系列新问题。公司选择这种部署策略可能有不同原因：

  • Following compliance regulations, where the data of one country’s users should reside in the same country’s data center
    遵循合规法规，即一个国家用户的数据应驻留在同一国家的数据中心
  • Increasing application resiliency so that the service operates without disruptions even if a cloud region goes down entirely
    提高应用弹性，使服务即使在某个云区域完全宕机时也能不中断地运行
  • Bringing applications nearer to the end users so that requests can be served faster
    把应用带到离终端用户更近的地方，以便更快地服务请求

Let’s assume the application is deployed in two AWS regions, and both serve the customer traffic depending on the geolocation of the customer. If one of the region’s services are impacted, the traffic is shifted to the functional region, and the customer experience is not affected, as shown in Figure 16-11.

假设应用部署在两个 AWS 区域，两个区域根据客户的地理位置服务客户流量。如果其中一个区域的服务受到影响，流量被切换到正常运行的区域，客户体验不受影响，如图 16-11 所示。

Page 460

Here are a few important considerations for service deployment in multiple regions:

以下是多区域服务部署的几个重要考量：

  • Both regions are completely functional and can independently serve the customer traffic. There are no common services between the regions.
    两个区域都完全可用，可以独立服务客户流量。区域之间没有公共服务。
  • The services are stateless, and the state is maintained only at the database layer. The information stored in the databases is continuously replicated to another region asynchronously (because user requests should not be affected due to replication lag). Either the database replication is inherently supported by the database, such as with DynamoDB global tables and the global data store for ElastiCache Redis, or you should implement it on your own if support is not available in the database.
    服务是无状态的，状态只维护在数据库层。数据库中存储的信息持续异步复制到另一个区域（因为用户请求不应因复制延迟而受影响）。数据库复制要么由数据库原生支持（例如 DynamoDB global tables 和 ElastiCache Redis 的全局数据存储），要么如果数据库不支持，你应自己实现。
  • Service deployments across the regions should be in sync with automation as much as possible. Additionally, consider keeping a buffer window between the same deployment on multiple regions. This helps identify any issues in one region before changes are propagated to another region.
    跨区域的服务部署应尽可能通过自动化保持同步。此外，考虑在多个区域的同一部署之间保留一个缓冲窗口。这有助于在变更传播到另一个区域之前，先在一个区域识别出任何问题。

In the scenario of region downtime, traffic should be shifted to another region, as shown in Figure 16-11. We recommend shifting this traffic gradually rather than in one go to avoid disruptions in another region due to increased traffic. The thundering herd problem can arise if all the clients switch to another region at the same time. Random jitter should be introduced in the client devices for API invocation to the server.

在区域宕机的场景下，流量应切换到另一个区域，如图 16-11 所示。我们建议逐步切换流量，而不是一次性全部切过去，以避免因流量增加而在另一个区域造成中断。如果所有客户端同时切换到另一个区域，可能出现惊群（thundering herd）问题。应在客户端设备中引入随机抖动，用于向服务器发起 API 调用。

Serving some users is better than serving none. For region failures, consider a load-shedding strategy to drop a percentage of requests to manage the load on a single region. The systems can eventually be scaled in the single region to serve all the traffic.

服务部分用户总比谁都不服务好。对于区域故障，考虑采用负载削减（load-shedding）策略，丢弃一定百分比的请求，以管理单个区域的负载。系统最终可以在单个区域内扩展到服务全部流量。

Page 461

Conclusion

Along with identifying system requirements and boundaries, it is very important to figure out user behavior and traffic patterns for how users interact with the platform. Our social networking system has two kinds of users—normal users with fewer followers and celebrity users with followers in the millions—and we segregated these two types for optimal design when building the user timeline.

除了识别系统需求和边界，弄清用户行为以及用户如何与平台交互的流量模式也非常重要。我们的社交系统有两类用户——粉丝较少的普通用户和粉丝数百万的名人用户——在构建用户时间线时，我们把这两类分开以做最优设计。

We also surfaced multiple examples of systems, starting with a simple architecture and then moving to a more complex one as new requirements come up or as the system scales for more users. One such example is managing the user relationships in databases like MySQL and later moving to a graph database to optimally figure out indirect relationships (such as the second-degree connections in LinkedIn). The same analogy applies to choosing a cloud provider service versus building the entire service on your own, as we described in our comparison of Cognito and a custom authentication solution.

我们还展示了多个系统示例，从简单架构开始，随着新需求出现或系统扩展到更多用户，再演进到更复杂的架构。其中一个例子是在 MySQL 之类的数据库中管理用户关系，后来迁移到图数据库以最优地找出间接关系（例如 LinkedIn 的二度人脉）。同样的类比也适用于选择云服务商服务 vs 自己构建整个服务，正如我们在 Cognito 与自定义认证方案的对比中所描述的。

In the next chapter, we’ll explore the design of another real-time system: an online gaming leadership board in multiplayer games. This chapter will introduce you to concepts around designing low-latency systems with multiple concurrent users playing at the same time.

下一章我们将探讨另一个实时系统的设计：多人游戏中的在线游戏排行榜。本章将向你介绍设计低延迟系统的相关概念，系统中有多个并发用户同时游玩。
